question: Keď tínedžeri povedia, že sa niekto „flexuje“ novým mobilom, myslia tým, že sa predvádza. Čo pôvodne „flexovali“ Angličania, keď sa chceli predviesť?
source_excerpt: to show off, whether it be your physique, your belongings, or some other thing you consider superior

extra.why_interesting: Parents hear their teenagers say someone 'flexuje' with new sneakers or a phone, and they take it as pure abstract slang. The picture behind it is a bodybuilder posing with a tensed arm. Players can work it out from the word 'flexibilný' or from the gym pose.
extra.verification_notes: Slang 'flex' (show off) is widely understood to derive from flexing muscles; no source contradicts this, though none explicitly states the origin (https://www.dictionary.com/browse/flex).

explanation: Anglické „to flex“ znamená napnúť svaly, ako to robia kulturisti s bicepsom, a odtiaľ sa výraz preniesol na akékoľvek predvádzanie sa.

question: Slovo „sus“, ktorým mladí označujú niečo podozrivé, sa rozšírilo vďaka online hre, v ktorej posádka vesmírnej lode hľadá medzi sebou zradcu. Ako sa tá hra volá?
source_excerpt: Among Us ... remained relatively under the radar until mid-2020, when it experienced an extraordinary surge in popularity. Players used 'sus' to accuse others of being impostors.

extra.why_interesting: Parents hear kids say 'to je sus' and assume it's just random teen-speak. Most don't know that a single cartoonish multiplayer game about finding a traitor on a spaceship spread it. The spaceship-and-traitor clue lets anyone who has seen kids play it work the answer out.
extra.verification_notes: Among Us (InnerSloth) popularized 'sus' in 2020, even though the word is older; the question says 'rozšírilo', which holds (https://dailydot.com/news/sus-meme/).

explanation: „Sus“ je skratka anglického „suspicious“, teda podozrivý. Celosvetovo sa udomácnilo cez Among Us, kde hráči hlasujú, koho z posádky vyhodia ako podvodníka.
